prompt: Draw a small transparent two-pose sprite sheet for an original historical pixel-art game. Two equal square cells in one horizontal row, one sprite centered per cell, with wide clear margins, no text or grid. The same adult 1940s infantry character wears a matte dark steel helmet and solid muted gray-green tunic and trousers, black boots and brown web gear. The first image is the exact sprite drawing style to match: distinct clean pixel clusters and natural proportions. The other images give reference for a period uniform and the shape of the carried prop. View from near front, with a slight turn to screen right. In the left cell he crouches low with one knee down, holding the compact dark historical prop diagonally low across his lap, elbows relaxed, silhouette low. In the right cell he is in a higher kneel with that same knee on the same baseline, shoulders and head raised, holding the same prop horizontally at chest height at a slight angle to screen right. Keep the exact same scale, helmet and face in both, clear glove shapes and both boots inside the frame. Calm archival figure study with two poses. Fully transparent background, no props outside the figure, no terrain, no effects, no captions.

historicalReferences.use: Gray steel helmet from the museum collection; no individual unit markings copied.

preparation.split: Two equal columns, left to right, no trimming of source before splitting.
preparation.resampling: Nearest neighbor, applied uniformly to each alpha crop.
preparation.alignment: Ground the bottom of both poses at anchor y and horizontally register the grounded knee.
